People.metaDescription: Twenty minutes with someone who uses the skill you’re watching. Free for students.
People.title: Ask someone who does the work.
People.lede: When a skill you follow moves, we find up to three people who use it every day and have 20 minutes free. You bring the decision you’re stuck on.
People.rulesTitle: Built so nobody is left hanging

optIn.title: Only people who opted in
optIn.body: Practitioners sign up themselves and confirm a work email. We never list anyone who hasn’t.

window.title: 72 hours to reply
window.body: If someone can’t make it or doesn’t answer within 72 hours, we quietly ask the next person. You’ll never see a “no”.

noShow.title: Both sides confirm
noShow.body: After the chat, both of you say whether it happened. Two no-shows in 30 days pauses matching for 30 days — for students and practitioners alike.

safety.title: Report or block, any time
safety.body: Every chat page has report and block. Recruiting, selling or anything that makes you uncomfortable breaks the code of conduct.

People.startEmptyTitle: Nothing on your watchlist is moving right now
People.startEmptyBody: You can still ask about any skill or role you follow — or browse the market for signals.
People.signInHint: Sign in to start from your own watchlist.
People.supplyAvailable: {n, plural, one {# practitioner} other {# practitioners}} with open times
People.supplyNote: We don’t publish a directory. You meet people through a signal, so every chat starts with context.
People.supplyDefinition: Counted from practitioners’ own availability in the last hour. Names aren’t listed on purpose.
People.joinTitle: Twenty minutes a month can change someone’s semester.
People.joinBody: Say which skills you use and when you’re free. You choose your monthly limit, you can pause any time, and declining needs no reason.

Starters.signal_rise: Ads mentioning {instrument} went from {from} to {to} in the last 4 weeks. Does that match what you see at work?
Starters.signal_fall: Ads mentioning {instrument} dipped from {from} to {to} recently. Is that noise, or is something shifting?
Starters.signal_entry: More entry-level ads mention {instrument} lately. Do juniors on your team use it from day one?
Starters.signal_since: {instrument} has moved since I started following it. What would you watch if you were me?
Starters.no_signal: Where does {instrument} actually come up in a normal week for you?
Starters.role_path: What would you tell someone aiming to become a {instrument} next year?
Starters.adjacent: I asked about {instrument}, and you use {adjacent}. How close are they in practice?
Starters.decision: Here’s what I’m deciding: {question}. What would you want to know before giving advice?
Starters.choosing_electives: If you were choosing units again, would you spend a semester on {instrument}? What would you pair it with?
Starters.grad_programs: How much did {instrument} matter when you applied for graduate roles?
Starters.internships: Would {instrument} have helped you get an internship, or is it something you learn on the job?
Starters.first_90_days: What do you wish you’d known about {instrument} in your first 90 days?
Starters.side_projects: What’s a small project I could build with {instrument} that would teach me the right things?
Starters.portfolio: What would make a {instrument} project stand out on a portfolio to you?
Starters.interview_prep: How does {instrument} come up in interviews for roles like yours?
Starters.visa_work_rights: Did work rights affect which employers you could apply to, and how did you handle it?
Starters.switching_into_tech: How did you learn {instrument} coming from outside a CS degree?
Starters.day_to_day: What does a normal week look like in your role, and where does {instrument} come in?

NewChat.title: Talk to someone who uses {name}
NewChat.lede: Twenty minutes, on a time they’ve opened. Nothing is sent until the last step.
NewChat.unknownBody: Pick a skill or role from the market to start a chat about it.
NewChat.questionHint: One or two sentences. The person you ask will see it, so be specific — it’s what makes 20 minutes useful.
NewChat.questionPlaceholder: e.g. COMP3xxx vs INFO3xxx next semester — and is it worth learning Rust on the side?

examples.units: COMP3xxx vs INFO3xxx next semester — which one sets me up better?
examples.grad: Should I apply for grad programs now, or get an internship first?
examples.switch: I’m in Commerce. Is it realistic to move into data engineering?

NewChat.questionTooShort: A little more, please — at least {min} characters.
NewChat.peopleLede: Up to three people, picked for the reasons listed on each card. No rankings — choose whoever fits your question.
NewChat.adjacentTitle: Nobody who uses {name} has time right now
NewChat.adjacentBody: These people use closely related skills and can speak to how {name} fits in. You can also join the waitlist and we’ll email you when someone who uses {name} opens times.
NewChat.waitlistTitle: Nobody has open times for {name} right now
NewChat.waitlistBody: That happens while we grow. Join the waitlist and we’ll email you the moment someone who uses {name} opens times. Nothing else is shared.
NewChat.waitlistJoinedBody: We’ll email you when someone opens times. You can leave the waitlist from My requests.
NewChat.waitlistRecruit: Know someone who uses {name}? Practitioners join in five minutes and choose how often they chat.
NewChat.openRequestTitle: You already have a live request about {name}
NewChat.openRequestBody: It’s {status}. You can still ask someone else — they won’t see each other’s requests.
NewChat.timeLede: All chats are 20 minutes. Times are at least two days away so {name} has time to reply.
NewChat.timeZoneNote: Times shown in your time zone ({tz}). {name} is in {theirTz}.
NewChat.timeZoneSame: Times shown in your time zone ({tz}), the same as {name}.
NewChat.noTimes: {name} has no open times in the next four weeks. Choose someone else.
NewChat.startersHint: Suggested from the signal, your decision and what {name} likes to talk about. Edit freely — they’re sent with your request.
NewChat.shareHint: Your name and decision are always shared. Choose anything else — defaults come from your privacy settings.
NewChat.shareSignal: The signal and filter you started from
NewChat.conduct: I’ll be respectful, keep to 20 minutes, and won’t ask for a job referral in the first chat.
NewChat.conductRequired: Please agree to the code of conduct to send.
NewChat.sentBody: They have up to 72 hours to reply. You don’t need to do anything.
NewChat.contextNoSignal: No signal — just curious. That’s fine.
NewChat.pausedTitle: New requests are paused for now
NewChat.pausedBody: After two missed chats in 30 days, requests pause for 30 days. This applies to everyone. See the no-show rules.
NewChat.shareOnlyName: Only your first name and decision.
NewChat.peopleChanged: That person or time isn’t available any more. Please choose again.

Chat.notFoundBody: It may belong to a different account, or the link is incomplete.
Chat.otherPersona: This chat belongs to your {persona} view.
Chat.waitingBody: You don’t need to do anything. If {name} can’t make it, we’ll quietly ask someone else and let you know.
Chat.stillLookingBody: {name} couldn’t make this one — that’s normal and not about you. We’ve passed your question on.
Chat.stillLookingWaitlist: Nobody else has time right now, so you’re on the waitlist. We’ll email you when someone opens times.
Chat.earlierNote: {n, plural, one {We asked one other person first} other {We asked # other people first}}. They didn’t have time.
Chat.newTimeBody: Your original time didn’t work for them. Take the new time, or say no and we’ll close this request.
Chat.newTimeDeclineConfirm: Close this request? {name}’s suggested time goes back on their calendar.
Chat.meetingLinkMissing: {name} will share a link by email before the chat.

prep.p1: Reread your decision. What would change your mind?
prep.p2: Pick the one opener you care most about and start there.
prep.p3: Look at {instrument} once more — the numbers you started from are linked below.
prep.p4: Have a note open. After the chat, you’ll get one click to say how it went.

Chat.cancelConfirmBody: The time goes back on {name}’s calendar. Cancelling at least 24 hours ahead doesn’t count against anyone.
Chat.cancelConfirmPending: Withdraw this request? {name} won’t be asked to reply.
Chat.cancelRule: You can cancel up to 24 hours before. After that, if something comes up, just join briefly or message them.
Chat.cancelTooLate: Less than 24 hours to go, so this can’t be cancelled here.
Chat.afterBody: One click is enough. Your answer goes into your notes on {instrument} — only you see it.
Chat.notePlaceholder: e.g. Learn window functions properly before applying
Chat.didntHappenBody: Tell us if {name} didn’t come. It’s kept private and only used for the no-show rules.
Chat.markAbsentConfirm: Mark {name} as absent? This is recorded for the no-show rules.
Chat.missedTitle: This chat was marked as missed
Chat.missedBody: It happens. Two missed chats in 30 days pauses new requests for 30 days.
Chat.didNotHappenBody: We’ve recorded it. You can ask someone else about {instrument} straight away.
Chat.cancelledBody: Nothing else to do. You can start a new request whenever you like.
Chat.safetyBody: Something off? Report it or block — the other person isn’t told who reported.
Chat.pSharedNone: {name} chose to share only their first name.
Chat.pExpires: Reply by {when} — after that we’ll pass it on for you.
Chat.pSuggestBody: Pick one of your open times. {name} gets 72 hours to take it.
Chat.pSuggestNone: You have no other open times at least 24 hours away. Add availability on your desk.
Chat.pDeclineBody: No reason needed. {name} won’t see that you declined — we’ll quietly pass the request to someone else.
Chat.pWaitingStudent: Waiting for {name} to take the new time ({when}).
Chat.pAttendanceBody: One click. It’s only used for the no-show rules.
Chat.pCancelRule: You can cancel up to 24 hours before; we’ll find {name} someone else.
Chat.pNoLink: Add a meeting link to your profile so {name} can join.
Chat.stillLookingNone: Nobody else has time right now. Try a related skill, or ask again in a few days.

Requests.title: My requests
Requests.lede: Everything you’ve asked, in one place. Nothing here is a score.
Requests.needsYouHint: A quick answer keeps things moving.
Requests.waitingHint: Nothing to do. We’ll email you when something changes.
Requests.emptyBody: Start from a signal on your watchlist, or from any skill you’re curious about.

groupEmpty.past: Finished chats will show up here.

Requests.rowStillLooking: On the waitlist — we’ll email you
Requests.waitlistRow: {name} — we’ll email you when someone opens times

PractitionerJoin.title: Twenty minutes, on your terms
PractitionerJoin.lede: Students find you through a market signal, so every request comes with context. You choose how often, when, and whether — declining needs no reason.
PractitionerJoin.agreeConduct: I’ve read and will follow the code of conduct — no recruiting, selling or asking students for anything.

agreePoints.p1: Students see your first name, title, employer, entry year, city, skills, topics and how you got in. Never your email.
agreePoints.p2: You set a monthly limit (1–4 chats). You can pause any time.
agreePoints.p3: If you don’t reply within 72 hours, the request quietly moves on. No penalty.
agreePoints.p4: Both sides confirm attendance. Two no-shows in 30 days pauses matching for 30 days.

PractitionerJoin.emailBody: We send a 6-digit code to your work email. We only keep the domain (e.g. company.com.au) to show you’re verified.
PractitionerJoin.codeSent: Code sent to {email}. It expires in 10 minutes.
PractitionerJoin.codePreview: Preview: the code is in Preview controls → Emails that would be sent.
PractitionerJoin.codeRemaining: {n, plural, one {# try left} other {# tries left}}
PractitionerJoin.freeMailTitle: That looks like a personal email
PractitionerJoin.freeMailBody: Personal and student addresses can’t confirm where you work. Use your work email, or ask for a manual review — a person checks your LinkedIn profile, usually within two working days.
PractitionerJoin.manualBody: We’ll check that your profile matches the job you list. You can finish your profile now; students can’t match with you until review is done.
PractitionerJoin.manualEmail: Email we can reach you at
PractitionerJoin.manualPending: Under review. You can keep setting up meanwhile.
PractitionerJoin.manualRejected: Your last review wasn’t approved. Try a work email, or submit again with more detail.
PractitionerJoin.profileBody: Keep it short and specific. This is what makes a match explainable.
PractitionerJoin.fRoleHint: Used for matching students who follow a role.
PractitionerJoin.fEmployerHint: Shown on your card. Employers never see anything about students.
PractitionerJoin.fEntryYear: Year you started working in the field
PractitionerJoin.fSkillsHint: Pick up to 12. You’ll be matched on these.
PractitionerJoin.fPathHint: One or two sentences — degree, internship, switch from another field…
PractitionerJoin.fPathPlaceholder: e.g. Graduate program after a Bachelor of IT; picked up Rust in a capstone.
PractitionerJoin.fBioPlaceholder: What you work on, in plain words.
PractitionerJoin.fLinkHint: Your own Zoom, Meet or Teams link. We don’t host video.
PractitionerJoin.fCapHint: We never match you with more than this.

fieldErrors.entry_year: Choose a year up to this year.
fieldErrors.path: Add a sentence on how you got in (10+ characters).

PractitionerJoin.availabilityBody: Set a weekly pattern. We turn it into 20-minute times for the next four weeks; students only see times at least two days away.
PractitionerJoin.doneBody: Students can now find you through signals. We’ll email you when someone asks.
PractitionerJoin.donePending: You’re set up. Students can match with you once your manual review is approved.

Availability.empty: No windows yet. Add one — even a single lunchtime a week helps.
Availability.slotsPerWeek: {n, plural, one {# chat time a week} other {# chat times a week}}
Availability.noSlots: No times in the next two weeks.

PractitionerDesk.title: Hi {name}
PractitionerDesk.lede: Requests, upcoming chats and your availability. Only you see this page.
PractitionerDesk.actingHint: Preview: answer requests as any fictional practitioner.
PractitionerDesk.suspended: Matching is paused until {date} after two missed chats. Existing chats are unaffected.
PractitionerDesk.unverified: Your manual review is pending — students can’t match with you yet.
PractitionerDesk.pausedNote: You’re paused. Students can’t send you new requests.
PractitionerDesk.inboxEmpty: No requests waiting. We’ll email you when someone asks.
PractitionerDesk.statsAcceptedDetail: Accepted chats with a time this month, against your monthly limit.
PractitionerDesk.statsSlotsDetail: 20-minute times from your weekly pattern, next four weeks.
PractitionerDesk.statsPrivate: Private to you. Students never see numbers about you or themselves.
PractitionerDesk.pauseHint: Booked chats still happen. Resume whenever.
PractitionerDesk.capLine: Up to {cap, plural, one {# chat} other {# chats}} a month

Safety.reportBody: Reports go to a person on our team. {name} isn’t told who reported.
Safety.detailsHint: What happened, and when. Required for “something else”.
Safety.detailsError: Please add a few words (10+ characters).
Safety.reportedBody: We review every report. If you’re in danger, call 000.
Safety.blockBody: You won’t be matched with each other again, and open requests between you are closed. {name} isn’t told.
Safety.unblockHint: You can unblock from your settings or desk.
Safety.urgent: If you’re in immediate danger, call 000.
